If the overlay window is removed (service stops, window detached) without `cancelAndClear` being called, the tick chain keeps firing every 40ms and calling `setText` on a detached view until the buffer drains; pending `View.post { scrollToBottom() }` actions also linger. Override `onDetachedFromWindow()` to `handler.removeCallbacks(typeTick)`.

**Finding 2 (Bug, medium): Dark-mode colors computed once in init; stale after dark-mode toggle.**
Anchor: the `val dark = ...` lines in init.

**Finding 3 (Bug, low-medium): typeNew leaves scroll/pin state stale.**
`BubbleScrollPolicy` starts with `pinnedToBottom = true`, so the initial state is fine. But if the user scrolled up (manual pin), and then a brand-new message arrives via `typeNew`, follow remains suspended and the view stays at the old scrollY (or even scrolled into emptied content) — the new message types without any scrolling, and the user must drag to bottom to resume. Per policy doc "新内容到达即滚到底", a fresh message should reset the pin state and scroll to top. BubbleScrollPolicy has no reset API, so BubbleView can't easily do it — mention: consider resetting `scrollPolicy` (add reset) and `scrollTo(0, 0)` in `typeNew`.

Hmm, wait — is that true? After `typeNew`: text="" → layout likely null or empty; scrollY stays whatever it was. As text grows via ticks, shouldAutoFollow() false → no scroll. The view height shrinks? maxHeight fixed; with less content height shrinks → TextView height change; scrollY clamped by layout... View.scrollTo doesn't auto-clamp, but TextView when layout changes... scrollY might stay > 0 making content offset weirdly. Either way, new message not visible from top and no auto-follow — real UX bug. Medium.

comments.content: Switch 内部状态与外部真实状态可能永久失步：onCheckedChange 中 `state = it` 在 onChecked 之后无条件执行，但 onChecked 的副作用可能被阻止而未生效。典型场景：悬浮窗开关在未授权时打开 —— onChecked(true) 分支只跳转权限页、不写 pref，父级 checked（overlayGranted && overlayEnabledPref）保持 false；由于 checked 未变化，remember(checked) 不会重置 state，用户从权限页返回后 Switch 仍显示为「开」，而实际 pref=false、服务未启动，状态错误直至某次 checked 值真正变化。建议改为无状态组件，直接由调用方回写的 checked 驱动 UI（本文件所有调用方在 onChecked 中均已回写状态，除被阻止的悬浮窗场景外均一致）。

comments.content: Index-based transcript baseline is fragile: `transcriptBaseline` captures `messages.value.size` once (remember has no keys, so it also resets on composition recreation), and the subtitle filter `messages.drop(transcriptBaseline)` assumes list indices stay stable for the whole session. If the VM trims/clears/rebuilds history during fullscreen mode (history cap, context reset) old assistant replies leak into the subtitle, or if history shrinks below the baseline all new replies are silently hidden (drop(n>size) yields an empty list). A message-identity baseline (e.g., remember the id/reference of the entry-time tail message and render only messages after it) is more robust; at minimum, coerce the baseline against the current size.
comments.existing_code: val transcriptBaseline = remember { chatVm.messages.value.size }

comments.content: Stale EMA seed across listening sessions: `listenRms` is only updated while LISTENING and never reset when the state exits, so each new listening turn seeds the waveform with the previous turn's final amplitude. With the ~120ms smoothing constant this produces a spurious initial burst in the 7-bar waveform before real audio arrives. Reset the level when entering LISTENING (or clamp on exit).

ThinkingDots runs three concurrent keep-alive mechanisms: (1) the withFrameNanos loop that actually advances `timeMs`, (2) a bare Choreographer re-post callback that does zero work at full refresh rate, and (3) an infinite 400ms heartbeat coroutine. Only (1) produces output; (2) and (3) are pure CPU/battery overhead on the very weak devices this screen targets, and the empty `doFrame` re-post keeps the frame pipeline hot even when the composable is invisible. Unless a specific OEM frame-pipeline stall was reproduced with (2)/(3) removed, drop both and rely on the single frame-clock driver.

comments.content: Two notes on the enter/exit pairing: (1) the `VoiceClientFactory.session(context)` warm-up call here is redundant — the identical singleton call already ran in `remember { VoiceClientFactory.session(context) }` earlier in composition, so this line is dead weight. (2) Both hide and restore silently no-op when `PetOverlayService.instance` is null (service not bound/died); no log is emitted, which weakens the documented enter/exit pairing contract and makes field debugging of a stuck/missing overlay hard. Log the degradation on both paths.

Divergent cancel entry points for the same user intent: pet double-tap calls `chatVm.cancelCurrentTurn()` while the drawer interrupt button calls `session.cancelCurrentTurn()`. Verified that the VM version is a unified gated router that delegates to VoiceSessionManager for voice rounds, so they are currently functionally equivalent — but keeping two different targets invites drift if the VM-side gating (voiceActive checks) changes and one path starts no-oping. Unify both interrupt entry points on one target.
